blurb: Shaggy little Highland terrier named for the stone cairns where it hunted vermin
description: The Cairn Terrier is a small working terrier from the Scottish Highlands with a harsh, weather-resistant double coat in cream, wheaten, red, gray or brindle.
answer: The Cairn Terrier is a small terrier from the Scottish Highlands and the Isle of Skye, counted among Scotland's earliest working dogs. It stands roughly 28 to 31 cm tall and weighs about 6 to 7.5 kg. Its name comes from the stone cairns where it flushed out vermin.

body: Before 1873, terriers in Scotland were collectively called Scottish Terriers. When the breed reached official UK shows in 1909 it was entered as the Short-haired Skye Terrier, but objections from Skye Terrier breeders led to the compromise name Cairn Terrier. The AKC registered the breed in 1903, the Kennel Club gave it a separate register in 1912, and the FCI definitively accepted it in 1963. After 1917 the AKC required white Cairns to be registered as West Highland White Terriers. The breed is now classed by the Kennel Club as a Vulnerable Native Breed.

The Cairn has a shaggy, harsh, weather-resistant outer coat over a soft, dense undercoat. Colors include cream, wheaten, red, sandy, gray and brindle; many kennel clubs do not permit pure black, black and tan, or white. Brindled Cairns often change color with age, becoming darker or more silver. A well-groomed Cairn still has a rough-and-ready look. It resembles the Norwich Terrier but has a shaggier coat.

The available sources say little about temperament. As a working terrier bred to flush vermin, it is commonly described by breed clubs in terms of its hunting background; prospective owners are best guided by the breed standard.

Sources give little detail on care. The double coat is meant to look natural and rough, and it is generally kept that way with regular brushing. Like most terriers, it is generally expected to enjoy daily activity.

Conditions reported in the breed include atopic dermatitis, cataracts, craniomandibular osteopathy, diabetes mellitus, hypothyroidism, Krabbe disease, Legg–Calvé–Perthes disease, luxating patella, ocular melanosis, portosystemic shunt, progressive retinal atrophy and von Willebrand disease. A 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 14 years, and a 2015 French study found 13.42 years.

faq.q: How big does a Cairn Terrier get?
faq.a: The ideal height is roughly 28 to 31 cm, with a weight of about 6 to 7.5 kg.

faq.q: How long do Cairn Terriers live?
faq.a: A 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 14 years, and a 2015 French study found 13.42 years.

faq.q: Why is it called a Cairn Terrier?
faq.a: The name comes from the cairns, or stone piles, where these terriers often flushed out vermin. It was adopted as a compromise name in 1909.

faq.q: Is the Cairn Terrier recognized by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. The FCI definitively accepted it in 1963, and it is breed number 4 in Group 3.
